I'm going to have to say Dota 2. Why?

It busted the world of eSports wide open for many gamers in the West. Captivating game play, exciting matches and pro-gamers, huge payouts, all that left gamers who were otherwise uninterested in watching others play games changing their minds and wanting more.

And the game itself is a massive success, even in spite of its difficulty curve and the time commitment required of its players.For what it is, Dota 2 is well designed, slick and just a lot of fun to play and watch. I think it's changed gaming itself, arguably more than pretty much any other game released since 2005.

Runners up?

  • Borderlands -- fun and addictive, the series does seem to be resting on its laurels with the pre-sequel. Hopefully BL4 will change that pace, but it's predecessors were fantastic.
  • Civilization V -- This has to be the topper for someone's list, right?
  • Path of Exile -- Oh, wow was this addictive. Rough around the edges, it's still compelling and exciting for hardcore gamers to sink their teeth into. I'd call it the anti-casual game done terribly right.

Games that didn't make the decade cut

  • WoW would've taken the cake if this started with 2004. Arguably, it's had the biggest and most enduring impact on the largest number of gamers during the last decade, all the same.
  • Neverwinter Nights -- More of a personal favorite, I still would argue that this was an important game because of the editing tools, the amazing and long-lived community surrounding it, and the endless fun it offered.
